newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korean Metals-Market quiet, hit by Hanbo scandal.
newsitem.headline: Korean Metals-Market quiet, hit by Hanbo scandal.

text.p: The South Korean metal market was quiet ahead of the Lunar New Year holiday with demand hit by recent labour unrest and the Hanbo Group loan scandal, traders said on Thursday.
The market was also jittery over rumours that LG Metals Corp was caught on the wrong side of London copper trading, despite the company's denial, traders said.
LG Metals' share price plunged on Wednesday to 12,300 won on the Seoul bourse, down 18 percent from last week's 15,000 won. On Thursday, it recovered to 13,300 won.
Hanbo Steel Co, flagship of the Hanbo Group, piled up about five trillion won ($5.7 billion) in loans from banks and financial institutions before its insolvency in late January.
Last Friday, South Korea's Office of Supply bought a total of 6,695 tonnes of aluminium at around 1.5 million won a tonne, traders said.
South Korean aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were firm at $90 to $95 a tonne CIF Pusan over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices, traders said.
Most domestic metal prices rose in lacklustre trading this week in line with the firm LME prices and the local currency's persistent decline against the dollar, they said.
Aluminium prices have risen to 1.51 million won a tonne from 1.45 million won a week earlier, while copper prices have fallen slightly to 2.279 million won from 2.286 million won.
Zinc prices rose by 59,000 won a tonne to 1.079 million won from 1.02 million a week ago and lead rose to 728,000 won from 706,000 won in the domestic market.
Most local metal importers were seen burdened by heavy losses from the won's stiff decline.

The won has plunged in line with the yen's weakness against the dollar on world markets and the country's snowballing trade deficit. The won fell to an 84-month low of 870.00 won against the dollar this week.
South Korea posted a record monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billion for January compared with $2.13 billion a year earlier.
